recipe.prompt: Act as an ad script editor. Check pacing, spoken voice, freshness and structure. Return JSON {scores:{pacing:1..5,spoken_voice:1..5,freshness:1..5,structure:1..5},notes:[short strings],edits:[{shot:int,text,vo,reason}]}. Edit only interior shots. Every revised line must match a supplied fact verbatim. Preserve timing. Prefer distinct concise lines that can be said in the allotted seconds.

shots.visual: Macro close-up in natural light. The tube cap opens and a dollop of aqua gel lands on a creator's fingertip. Hands only, no heavy edit.
Slow macro of a finger spreading the gel so its consistency and movement show. Product name card on screen.
Split-frame, real time. Left: gel dotted across the cheek. Right: fingertips blending it in. Natural light, hands only.
Tight close-up of the cheek after blending. Fingertips lightly touch the skin to show the finished surface. Soft natural light.
Clean product-in-hand shot, tube held steady to camera with the SPF 50+ PA++++ label legible. Hold still for the final beat.

facts.text: Watermelon Sunscreen SPF 50+ PA++++ With New-Age UV Filters For Oily Skin
Instant cooling sunscreen for luminous, sun protected skin
Supercharged with Watermelon, Hyaluronic Acid & UV Filters
Provides oil-free hydration while reducing uneven skin tone
Blocks UVA+UVB+blue light rays to check tanning & sun burn
Aqua gel & quick-absorbing, it blends seamlessly with zero white cast
Aqua-Gel Non-Oily Finish Lightweight Oily & Combination Skin melon
Apply on face, neck & other body parts
Use it even when indoors, or out on a cloudy day

notes: Structure works: texture hook, name, blend proof, finish proof, hold on the label. Each beat has one job.
Pacing is even. Short lines fit every slot, and nothing is crammed into the 2s opener or the 3s close.
Shots 2-4 repeat on-screen text word for word in the VO. That wastes spoken seconds and sounds like a label read aloud.
Shots 3 and 4 have room for a second distinct benefit in the VO, so the viewer hears something new beyond what they read.
Shot 2's VO is the product name, which the name card already shows. A cooling cue fits the slow gel spread better.
Shot 5 shows SPF 50+ PA++++ on the label, but the line is generic. It is an end shot, so I left it untouched. 'Explore the formula.' is a weak CTA.
Edits keep the on-screen text and change only the VO, so each VO is a verbatim fact. Timing is unchanged.

edits.reason: The name card already carries the product name. A cooling cue matches the slow gel spread and gives the viewer a new fact. It is 2 words, so it fits 3.5s.
The split-frame shows the gel blending in, so the VO describes the action while the on-screen text proves the result. The two no longer repeat each other.
The visual is fingertips touching the finished skin, so a tactile word fits. It adds a new benefit without repeating the on-screen claim, and it is easy to say in 4s.
